en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 8.6. Nahetusahetukaduka (The Pair on That Which is Without Cause but With Cause)
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, by way of root-condition:

dependent on one great primary element, the other three great primary elements arise … [as before] … Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor without a root, by way of root-condition:
at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the physical basis, states that are neither roots but accompanied by roots [arise].

Aggregates. Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root, there arise states that are neither-root nor accompanied-by-root and states that are neither-root nor rootless, by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless, there arises a state that is neither-root nor rootless, by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor rootless, there arises a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root,

by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor rootless, there arise states that are both neither a root nor accompanied by a root and neither a root nor rootless, by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor root-cause and a state that is neither-root nor non-root-cause, a state that is neither-root nor root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor root-cause and a state that is neither-root nor non-root-cause, a state that is neither-root nor non-root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
[Dependent on] a state that is neither-root nor root-cause and a state that is neither-root nor non-root-cause...

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, states that are neither a root nor accompanied by a root, and states that are neither a root nor not accompanied by a root, arise by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine for the root; four for the object; five for the predominance … pe … six for mutuality … pe … two for prenascence and repetition … pe … nine for non-disappearance.
(The “Conascent” section … pe … and the “Associated” section are also similar to the “Dependent” section.)

A state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root. A state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not a root but is not without a root.
A state that is neither a root nor without a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor without a root.

A state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause. (Abbreviated. Four in the case of the object; ... pe ...
four in the case of the immediate; ... pe ... seven in the case of co-nascence; six in the case of mutuality; seven in the case of dependence; four in the case of decisive support;
two each in the cases of prenascence, postnascence, and repetition; [two] in the case of kamma; ... pe ... four in the case of jhāna.
With the path, three; with association, two; with dissociation, three ... pe ... with non-disappearance, seven.
The Root Group is finished.
